name: Alaska Commercial Electronics, LLC
old_description: Marine Electronics Sales, Service, & Installation in Petersburg, Alaska.
about:
Alaska Commercial Electronics (ACE) has operated from Petersburg, Alaska since its founding in 1986 by Jerry Whitethorn and Richard Tamblin. The partners built a dedicated facility in 1994 that remains the company's base. In 2017, ownership transferred to Eric and Adele Rosvold as the founders transitioned to retirement, with technicians Megan O'Neil and Cynthia Benitz joining to continue the service legacy.

ACE sells, services, and installs marine electronics from brands including Nobeltec/TimeZero, Furuno, Icom, Morad, Simrad, and Comnav. The company also provides marine electrical services such as AC/DC installation, panel replacement, and vessel alarm systems. Historically, ACE designed industrial control systems for water treatment, power, and sewer treatment plants, built a solar-powered mountain-top radio repeater for wireless remote control of a hydro-electric plant, and in 1994 produced the Watch Clock, a microprocessor-based vessel watch alarm still in service decades later.

The primary customer base is Southeast Alaska's commercial fishing fleet, which operates from California to the Aleutian Islands. ACE also serves onshore industrial clients, including municipal water and wastewater utilities, power generation facilities, and remote telecommunications sites.

The company emphasizes that reliable equipment and timely repair are critical during short fishing openings and hostile conditions. Its guiding principles are captured in the statements "Serving our customers is our number one priority" and "We service what we sell," with professional installation offered in Alaska or anywhere on the West Coast.

about:
Alaska Shirt Company operates a retail store in Juneau, Alaska, positioned directly across from the Mount Roberts Tramway entrance. The shop serves visitors arriving by cruise ship at the CT, Franklin, and AJ docks, offering a convenient stop within minutes of the waterfront.

The company curates a selection of Alaska-themed merchandise, including t-shirts, sweatshirts, hoodies, long-sleeve shirts, jewelry such as earrings, necklaces, and pendants, as well as accessories, home and garden items, and gifts. The assortment emphasizes a range of sizes, styles, and colors to appeal to a broad audience of travelers and residents.

Its primary customers are cruise passengers and tourists exploring downtown Juneau, though the store also welcomes local shoppers seeking authentic Alaskan souvenirs. The location near the tram makes it a natural first stop for visitors disembarking at the nearby docks.

Alaska Shirt Company states that it differentiates itself by carefully curating its product mix to ensure appeal across age groups, maintaining a welcoming environment with staff available to assist, and prioritizing a pleasant shopping experience that encourages repeat visits.

name: Alaskan Outdoor Wearhouse
old_description: We proudly carry a variety of mens and womens outerwear suitable for rainy days in the Tongass.
about:
Capital Embroidery has provided embroidery services in Juneau, Alaska, for over a decade. The business has operated from several locations—downtown, then Lemon Creek—before settling in the Mendenhall Mall. Current owner Shane Walker expanded the operation to include a retail arm, Alaskan Outdoor Wearhouse & Embroidery (AOWE), which sells outdoor apparel and gear alongside the embellishment services.

The company offers custom embroidery and screen printing, handling orders ranging from single-name left-chest designs to large corporate logos on the backs of jackets and hoodies. Screen printing is offered as an alternative for lighter items or when waterproofing must be preserved. In addition to embellishment, AOWE stocks a range of outerwear, footwear, and accessories from vendors such as Western Chief, Wanakome, Oakiwear, and Prison Blues. Garments can be sourced through the distributor Sanmar, or customers may supply their own items after signing a waiver.

Customers include Alaska residents and businesses across the state. The shop has produced boat-themed embroidery for marine operators and corporate apparel for companies needing branded jackets. The retail side caters to outdoor enthusiasts seeking rainwear, boots, and cold-weather gear.

The business positions itself as a flexible local partner, offering both decoration and garment procurement under one roof. In 2023, Capital Embroidery & AOWE earned a silver award in the Best of Juneau competition.

about:
Alba Energy of Katy operates from its office in Katy, Texas. The company is part of a broader network with locations in Austin, Dallas, Houston, McAllen, and San Antonio, serving the greater Houston area including Brookshire, Sugar Land, and surrounding communities. No founding year or ownership details are publicly disclosed.

The firm specializes in residential solar panel installation and related services. Its offerings include site assessment, system design, installation, and ongoing production monitoring. Alba Energy promotes zero-upfront-cost options and financing programs structured to deliver savings from the first month. Each installation is backed by a 25-year manufacturer's warranty on equipment.

The primary customer base consists of homeowners in Texas seeking to reduce electricity costs through solar power. The company assists clients in claiming the federal investment tax credit, which can cover up to 30% of system costs. Service territories center on the CenterPoint Energy footprint in the Houston region.

Alba Energy differentiates itself with a "Peace-of-Mind Production Monitoring" platform, bilingual Spanish-English support, and a focus on customer education. Testimonials highlight reduced monthly bills and responsive service.

name: Albuquerque Fashion Incubator
old_description: The Albuquerque Fashion Incubator offers a one-of-a-kind, hands-on training opportunity in sewn product manufacturing. It is the only one of its kind in the world. Really.
about:
Albuquerque Fashion Incubator (ABQFI) operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico, where it has hosted apparel manufacturing boot camps since 2015. The program was founded by Kathleen Fasanella, principal of Apparel Technical Services and the Albuquerque Sewing Factory, who brings nearly four decades of production experience. Organized as a 501(c)3 non-profit, ABQFI began with a single “Coats for Kids” event and now runs two annual cycles of pre-production and production camps at the Albuquerque Sewing Factory on Old Coors Drive.

The incubator’s core activity is a four-day, hands-on boot camp that takes participants through the full sewn-product manufacturing process: pattern creation, production pattern auditing, work-instruction development, fabric spreading, cutting, sewing, and finishing. Each cycle includes a pre-production camp roughly three months before the production camp; attendees who register for pre-production are automatically enrolled in the production phase. Camps are capped at 25 participants, and the inaugural event produced 125 fully lined winter coats in four days using industrial equipment at the factory.

The training targets entrepreneurs, aspiring designers, and individuals with no prior factory experience—75 percent of the first cohort had never used an industrial machine. Finished garments are donated to qualified New Mexico charities serving children, seniors, and other underserved groups. The program also offers custom boot camps for larger groups by arrangement.

Fasanella launched the incubator to address the loss of domestic production knowledge, arguing that re-shoring requires people who know how to run factories. The model combines free instruction (participants cover only material costs) with charitable output, positioning ABQFI as a unique workforce-development and community-service hybrid.

name: All Electric Supply Inc.
old_description: A third-generation family business founded in 1957 by Roy T. Beard, Jr. in Little Rock,
about:
All Electric Supply Inc. is a third-generation, family-owned electrical distributor founded in 1957 by Roy T. Beard Jr. in Little Rock, Arkansas. The company began as a local supplier for contractors and builders in central Arkansas.

The firm stocks and distributes a broad range of electrical products, including Maxlite LED lamps, GE ballasts and fluorescent lamps, Eaton and Cutler-Hammer breakers, Cooper wiring devices, and EMT, PVC, and Sealtite connectors. It operates a will-call counter and offers local delivery, while its sales staff provides technical troubleshooting and helps source specialty items not kept in stock.

All Electric Supply primarily serves regional electrical contractors, builders, and commercial facilities. The company is also a Trade Ally for Entergy’s Commercial Energy Efficiency Programs, assisting commercial customers with energy-saving upgrades.

The company differentiates itself with a triple guarantee: will-call orders ready in 45 minutes or less, 100 percent order accuracy, and local delivery within 24 hours. Its heritage, tracing back to the founder’s ancestor Nanyehi (Nancy Ward), a Cherokee leader, is cited as a cultural touchstone for stewardship and cooperation.

about:
All Molded Plastics operates from Wallingford, Connecticut, where it was founded as a family-owned corporation. The company's history notes that operations began in the state, though a specific founding year is not disclosed. The business remains under family ownership and serves as a domestic manufacturing partner for custom plastic components.

The shop specializes in injection molding, compression molding, and transfer molding of both thermoplastic and thermoset compounds. It produces custom plastic parts, including large housings and covers molded in high-density polyethylene (HDPE), and offers finished-goods assembly services. The facility has expanded to accommodate larger injection molding machinery to meet growing customer demand.

All Molded Plastics works with a range of clients, notably nationally known distributors, supplying molded parts for various industrial and commercial applications. The company positions itself as a resource for American manufacturing, quoting projects from prototype through production runs.

The company emphasizes its role as a U.S.-based manufacturer, highlighting domestic production capabilities and a family-owned structure that supports responsive service.

name: All Steel Inc
old_description: All Steel Inc. is a Leading Provider of Metal Roofing Systems and Building Supplies
about:
All Steel Inc. operates two manufacturing facilities in Fairbanks and Wasilla, Alaska. The company was founded in 1998 as a family-owned business by Michael P. Kralman and his mother, Sandra M. Kralman.

The company manufactures metal roofing systems, metal wall panels, and a range of light gauge steel components including roofing, trim flashings, soffit, studs, track, and complete steel buildings. It also produces gutters, downspouts, elbows, and distributes IKO architectural and 3-tab roofing shingles. A custom roll forming machine was built in-house for a complex commercial project.

All Steel serves commercial and residential contractors across Alaska. Notable projects include fabricating up to 46 cold-formed steel trusses per week for Eielson Air Force Base and supplying custom-colored flashings and curved framing for the Chief Andrew Isaac Clinic. The company also supports general building and renovation projects throughout the state.

The founders started the business to address Alaska's short summer construction season, which makes ordering from out-of-state suppliers impractical. They emphasize quick turnaround, maintaining stock on hand, and a local workforce that understands the region's environmental extremes. The family-owned structure and in-house manufacturing capability allow them to control quality and respond to custom requirements.
